cases.scenario: Submit a structurally valid selection whose active input points at the entire repository and whose passive context points at all conversation history.
inputRisks: A fabricated reference can authorize context that the natural-language analyzer never inspected.
An unconstrained passive reference can silently broaden selection beyond catalog metadata.
expectedBehavior: Accept only task-session evidence references produced by the current analyzer invocation.
Require passiveContextRefs to identify the catalog metadata boundary and reject source, history, skill-body, or run-artifact references.
Prove active references came from the current request or explicitly attached artifacts.
forbiddenBehavior: Accept source://entire-repository as active selection evidence.
Accept all-history as passive selection context.
Treat an arbitrary non-empty string as authority to load context.
findings: The schema constrains reference fields only as non-empty strings and the validator adds no semantic ownership or allowlist checks.
A black-box invocation containing activeInputRefs=['source://entire-repository'] and passiveContextRefs=['all-history'] returned valid=true.
evidence: analyze-input.md: Allowed context limits passive inspection to skills/catalog.json metadata.
analyze-input.schema.json: activeInputRefs and passiveContextRefs items have only type and minLength constraints.
validate-analyze-input.mjs: validatorFor is called without semantic validation.

cases.scenario: Invoke a diagnostic skill with targetRefs=['*'], writeRoots=['/'], externalMutation=true, approvalRef=null, and invented request, artifact, and evidence references.
inputRisks: A schema-valid envelope can launder an unapproved mutation into a read-only flow.
Wildcard targets and a filesystem-root write boundary permit implicit scope expansion.
Invented evidence references can be mistaken for observed proof.
expectedBehavior: Correlate externalMutation=true with a current approval reference.
Reject wildcard targets, broad roots, foreign references, and references not selected by global analysis.
Bind requestRef and activeInputRefs to the same current task-session identity.
forbiddenBehavior: Accept writeRoots=['/'] or targetRefs=['*'].
Accept externalMutation=true with approvalRef=null.
Accept invented evidence and context references solely because they are non-empty strings.
findings: All materialized skill validators are schema-only; the local prose says to reject these conditions but executable validation does not enforce them.
A black-box starci-workflow-diagnose envelope containing the listed broad scope and null approval returned valid=true.
evidence: skills/starci-workflow-diagnose/input.schema.json: scope values are structurally closed but targetRefs and writeRoots are arbitrary non-empty strings.
skills/starci-workflow-diagnose/validate-input.mjs: no semantic callback is supplied.

skills/starci-frontend-layout-delivery/analyze-input.md: prose requires rejection of out-of-scope roots and unapproved external mutation, demonstrating the enforcement gap is cross-cutting rather than intentional.

cases.scenario: Inject an undeclared top-level field, an undeclared payload field, or caller-authored data into runtime loads.
inputRisks: Copied prompt context can enter an operator through a catch-all field.
The caller can replace a runtime-resolved binding with hallucinated content.
Provided facts and loaded context can become indistinguishable.
expectedBehavior: Reject every undeclared root and payload property.
Require payload.provided, payload.loads, and payload.session as separate closed objects.
Document who authors each section and forbid copied documents in reference fields.
forbiddenBehavior: Accept context, notes, prompt, relatedFiles, or arbitrary metadata bags.
Allow workers to populate or broaden payload.loads.
Infer a substitute when a provided reference cannot be resolved.
findings: Bulk inspection found 85 of 85 operator input schemas closed at both root and payload levels.
All 85 require payload.provided, payload.loads, and payload.session.
Every input document contains a JSON architecture section; the standardized families explicitly distinguish previous-state data from runtime loads.
evidence: operators/fe/grammar-convergence/input.md: separates Provided by the previous state from Loaded by the runtime and forbids inferred substitutes.
operators/be/repair-prerequisite-check/input.md: names exact metadata bindings and forbids source content and broad repository context.
operators/business/staleness-check/input.md: permits metadata only and lists prohibited semantic bodies.

cases.scenario: A coordinator or worker executes one step without relying on prior conversation to infer what it may read, retain, write, or use for a stop decision.
inputRisks: Vague words such as relevant or related can trigger broad retrieval.
A worker can mistake session analysis for authority or persist hidden reasoning.
An omitted write boundary can be interpreted as permission to mutate.
expectedBehavior: Every step names Read, Context, Session write, Durable write, Stop, and Orchestration behavior or explicitly declares the item inapplicable.
Context names exact bindings, revisions, or hashes rather than broad subject areas.
Workers receive immutable slices and the coordinator alone joins or commits.
forbiddenBehavior: Load related context or source as needed.
Persist worker prompts, transcripts, or hidden reasoning.
Assume mutation authority from an omitted durable-write statement.
findings: All 85 execute documents contain explicit Read, Context, Session write, and Stop markers, which sharply limits hallucinated retrieval.

Forty-one execute documents do not use an explicit Durable write marker and fourteen do not use an explicit Orchestration marker. Many state the same boundary elsewhere, but a harness cannot prove uniform interpretation from prose alone.
The remaining vague-word hits are mostly negative boundaries such as unrelated context; no broad as-needed context instruction was found.
evidence: operators/fe/grammar-convergence/execute.md: each step enumerates reads, context, decision evidence, writes, stops, and orchestration.
operators/fe/preflight/execute.md: metadata-only context and coordinator-only execution are explicit.
operators/be/coding-scope-freeze/execute.md: explicit read/context/session-write/stop language is present but the Durable write and Orchestration labels are not uniformly used.

cases.scenario: Select grammarId=core while attempting to load Offset Pop guidance, all object guides, or an unlisted knowledge identifier.
inputRisks: Mixed Grammar variants can produce fabricated render rules.
Loading every named case wastes context and creates conflicting instructions.
Usage guidance can be mistaken for executable npm authority.
expectedBehavior: Load Common overview and contracts, the selected Grammar overview, and only triggered object or named-case guides.
Reject every guide from the unselected Grammar.
Treat the installed npm package manifest, export map, version, integrity, and contract hash as executable authority.
forbiddenBehavior: Load core and offset-pop object rules together.
Retrieve all 34 registered guides for one layout.
Invent an export, prop, state, wrapper, or extension axis from usage prose.
findings: The input schema enumerates every legal guide ID and caps one invocation at twelve guides.
Semantic validation requires Common overview/contracts, the selected overview, at least one selected object or case, and rejects the other Grammar prefix.
The execution text explicitly distinguishes npm implementation authority from usage guidance.
evidence: operators/fe/grammar-convergence/input.schema.json: knowledge IDs are an enum with minItems=4 and maxItems=12.
operators/fe/grammar-convergence/validate-input.mjs: selectedPrefix and otherPrefix checks enforce variant isolation.
operators/fe/grammar-convergence/input.schema.json and execute.md Step 3 define conditional guide retrieval and npm authority.

cases.scenario: Emit a valid decision with a contradictory payload.state status, code, retryability, emitted route, or fact delta.
inputRisks: The parent machine can route on one state while the prose or decision claims another.
A blocked operator can masquerade as complete.
Hallucinated fact additions can unlock an unauthorized branch.
expectedBehavior: Correlate decision, root stage/status, operator status/code/retryability, emitted stage/status, and fact deltas.
Reject a non-success result that claims a durable mutation.
Require session ownership for produced and evidence references.
forbiddenBehavior: Accept decision=fresh with payload.state.code=business-staleness-blocked.
Accept decision=frozen with payload.state.status=blocked.
Accept decision=updated with an emits status unrelated to the decision.
findings: Eighty-two operator validators contain explicit decision-to-route correlation logic or equivalent generated checks.

business/staleness-check, fe/context-sync, and fe/coding-scope-freeze correlate root stage/status with decision in schema conditionals but do not correlate payload.state status, code, retryability, emitted route, or facts with that decision.
Those three schemas enumerate each field independently, so contradictory combinations remain structurally valid.
evidence: operators/fe/grammar-convergence/validate-output.mjs: demonstrates the expected full correlation contract.
operators/business/staleness-check/validate-output.mjs: checks only freshnessReceiptRef correlation.
operators/fe/context-sync/validate-output.mjs: checks durable writes and generation refs but not state correlation.
operators/fe/coding-scope-freeze/validate-output.mjs: checks only that frozen has a scope ref and targets.

cases.scenario: Return result=complete, finalState=banana, and receiptRefs=['invented:proof'] from a materialized skill.
inputRisks: An arbitrary finalState can hide a route that never reached a terminal.
An invented non-session receipt can falsely prove completion.
A generic output description gives the model no skill-specific terminal contract.
expectedBehavior: Restrict finalState to terminal state IDs declared by that skill machine.
Correlate result with the selected machine terminal.
Require typed, owned, evidence-bearing receipt references appropriate to that terminal.
Document the output JSON architecture and each terminal outcome.
forbiddenBehavior: Accept an arbitrary non-empty finalState.
Accept an invented receipt string as completion proof.
Use the same three-line output prose for every materially different skill.
findings: All 26 skill output documents contain the same generic sentence and do not enumerate JSON fields, terminal states, or result-specific evidence.
Skill output schemas define finalState and receiptRefs as arbitrary non-empty strings.
Validators only require at least one receipt when result is complete; a black-box frontend-layout output with finalState=banana and receiptRefs=['invented:proof'] returned valid=true.
evidence: skills/starci-frontend-layout-delivery/output.md: generic three-line output description.
skills/starci-frontend-layout-delivery/output.schema.json: finalState and receiptRefs lack machine-state and URI ownership constraints.
skills/starci-frontend-layout-delivery/validate-output.mjs: only checks that complete has a non-empty receiptRefs array.

cases.scenario: Reach a terminal, purge all task-session intermediates as instructed, then return receiptRefs to the caller.
inputRisks: Returned receipt references can point to objects deleted before the caller reads them.
The model can persist receipts to avoid the dangling-reference problem, violating session-only retention.
The word immutable can be mistaken for durable.
expectedBehavior: Define whether each returned receipt is a durable approved product artifact or a terminal response value copied before purge.
Never return a reference whose target is purged at the same terminal.
Make retention and ownership machine-checkable.
forbiddenBehavior: Purge a receipt and return only its now-dangling session URI.
Persist all receipts merely because output.md calls them immutable.
Leave receipt lifetime to model interpretation.
findings: Every generic skill execute document says to purge all task-session intermediates at every terminal, while every output document asks for immutable receipt references.
Neither the skill schema nor output prose distinguishes durable receipt identities from session-only receipts, so the intended lifetime is not provable from the contract.
evidence: skills/starci-frontend-layout-delivery/execute.md: terminal handling purges all task-session intermediates.
skills/starci-frontend-layout-delivery/output.md: asks for immutable receipt references without defining retention.
INDEX.md: operator receipts are ephemeral task-session objects unless an explicitly approved product-source or external mutation survives.

cases.scenario: Ask an early design or planning operator to inspect the whole repository because a generated contract candidate is incomplete.
inputRisks: The model can bypass canonical generated context and consume an entire codebase.
A missing candidate can be treated as permission to scan related files.
Stale hashes can be ignored in favor of remembered source.
expectedBehavior: Use metadata and hash-pinned generated contract records before coding scope is frozen.
Stop or refresh the canonical generation on hash mismatch.
After freeze, read only exact declared paths and verify their hashes.
forbiddenBehavior: Load rawRepositoryContext or repositoryContext=true.
Open an undeclared source file because it appears related.
Use generated or remembered content whose generation identity no longer matches.
findings: The source-facing contracts consistently forbid broad repository context and bind generated records or exact targets by hash.
Coding-scope operators explicitly prevent file bodies from entering context before scope freeze.
Implementation text requires returning to planning when another file or rule appears necessary.
evidence: operators/fe/context-sync/input.md: distinguishes canonical generated artifacts from model-visible raw source.
operators/fe/coding-scope-freeze/input.md: file bodies are forbidden and candidates must be rebound to the canonical generation.
operators/be/coding-scope-freeze/execute.md: hash-only readers never place bytes or text in model, worker, logs, output, or scratch context.
operators/be/implementation/execute.md: no additional source may be loaded after scope binding.

cases.scenario: Search execution and routing prose for open-ended retrieval instructions and vague references that could justify loading more context or changing another boundary.
inputRisks: Words such as relevant, related, appropriate, or as needed can authorize hallucinated dependencies.
A pronoun without a stable identity can refer to the wrong artifact or state.
A multi-capability request can silently execute later capabilities without a handoff.
expectedBehavior: Use exact refs, roles, revisions, hashes, stages, decisions, and owners.
Use vague scope words only in explicit negative boundaries or with a defined qualifier.
Require a new selection after an explicit handoff for later capabilities.
forbiddenBehavior: Load related context as needed.
Apply appropriate changes without naming the approved boundary.
Continue into a second capability merely because it seems useful.
findings: No as needed, if needed, where needed, appropriate, reasonable, current context, existing context, available context, all context, or full context instruction was found in operator prose.
The few relevant and necessary occurrences are qualified by explicit decisions, hashes, or stop boundaries.
Global analysis explicitly selects the first required capability and requires a new selection after an explicit handoff.
evidence: analyze-input.md: selection procedure step 3 prohibits silently executing later capabilities.
operators/be/implementation/execute.md: another necessary file makes the approved boundary insufficient and triggers replanning.
operators/fe/customer-journey/execute.md: journey-relevant authority is named as a bounded projection rather than an open repository scan.

topRisks: Global and skill-level validators accept fabricated reference identities and do not enforce the prose-defined context boundary.
Skill-level scope validation permits wildcard targets, root write boundaries, and external mutation without approval.
Skill outputs accept arbitrary terminal-state and receipt strings, allowing false completion proof.
Three operator outputs do not fully correlate payload.state with decision and emitted route.
Terminal cleanup and returned receipt lifetime are not explicitly reconciled.
